column1: MILE 12 WARRIOR  |  Content Gap & White Space Analysis
Demand that exists in the USA market which no competitor currently satisfies well. This is where Mile 12 Warrior wins fastest.

column3: No competitor of any size has a content hub for spouses, partners, kids and friends of drivers. 'Social Butterflies' is a genuine category with real search demand and effectively zero competition.
column4: Build /social-butterflies into a full pillar with 8-12 supporting pages. Fastest authority win on the entire site.

column2: Free fleet packets with sign-off sheets
column3: Rolling Strong and NAFMP charge or gate. Carrier blogs are recruiting funnels. Nobody offers a free, print-ready, DQ-file-compliant orientation packet.
column4: This is the B2B lead magnet. Gate lightly (email only), add schema, pitch directly to safety directors on LinkedIn.

column3: FMCSA owns the regulation. Nobody owns the translation. 'What the 14-hour rule actually means when you're stuck at a dock' is unclaimed.
column4: Every compliance page should pair the citation with a real-world worked example. That is the differentiator AI engines reward.

column3: TruckersReport, Life As A Trucker, Smart Trucking and most carrier blogs run little to no FAQPage, HowTo or ItemList schema.
column4: Ship FAQPage + HowTo schema on every page from day one. Immediate advantage in AI Overviews, ChatGPT and Perplexity citations.

column3: The new-driver SERP is owned by carrier recruiting blogs. A driver-owned, non-recruiting voice is a trust vacuum.
column4: Position /new-driver explicitly as 'no recruiter wrote this'. Say it on the page. It is the whole angle.

column3: Most fatigue content stops at 'get enough sleep'. NAFMP is a 2013 slide deck. Nobody publishes an actual usable protocol.
column4: Own /fatigue-management as the definitive practitioner guide with named protocols, timings and decision rules.

column3: Almost no competitor gives away print-ready checklists that live in the cab.
column4: Every checklist becomes a page + PDF + schema. Print assets earn backlinks and repeat visits that pure articles do not.

column3: Chain control levels, Title 13 CCR, CHP enforcement and CA-vs-federal HOS differences are poorly covered by anyone.
column4: Own the CA layer. It is the local anchor, it is winnable, and out-of-state drivers search it constantly before a run.

column3: Competitors are either institutions with no lived experience or bloggers with no credentials. Mile 12 Warrior has both.
column4: Put the founder's name, face, years and route history on every page. Add Person + author schema. This is the single strongest E-E-A-T asset the site has and it is currently underused.

column2: Forum + expert content on one domain
column3: TruckersReport has community with no authority. Life As A Trucker has authority with no community. Nobody has both on one domain.
column4: The forum and the roadmap reinforce each other: expert pages rank, forum threads capture long-tail and dwell time. Interlink them deliberately.

column2: Mental health without stigma or sales
column3: Most mental-health trucking content is written by insurers, WiFi vendors or factoring companies with a product attached.
column4: A driver talking to drivers about depression, with crisis resources and no product, is uniquely citable and uniquely shareable.

column3: No competitor publishes a 12-month hazard calendar drivers can plan against.
column4: Build it as an interactive page. Naturally refreshed every year, naturally linkable, naturally seasonal traffic.

column3: AI engines cite statistics constantly. Trucking safety and health stats are scattered across PDFs and studies.
column4: Build one cited, updated statistics hub. Highest-ROI single page for AI citation and journalist backlinks.

column3: Effectively zero competitors in this vertical have implemented llms.txt or optimised for AI crawler consumption.
column4: Ship llms.txt, clean semantic HTML, entity markup and answer-first page structure. First-mover advantage is real and currently free.
